title: A protocol to assess cellular bioenergetics in flavivirus-infected cells
protocol: Culture an appropriate number of MRC-5 cells (minimum 2.4 × 10^6 cells).
Dilute the cultured cells to a concentration of 2 × 10^5 cells/mL using EMEM GM.
Add 500 μL of cell suspension into each well of Seahorse XF 24-well plates, resulting in 1 × 10^5 cells/well per well.
Tap the sides of the plate gently to distribute the cell suspension evenly.
Incubate the plates at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 18-24 hours to allow cell attachment and growth.
Check the viability of cells prior to starting the experiment using a conventional light microscope.
Ensure that more than 90% of the wells have confluent monolayers with minimal well-to-well variability.
Subject MRC-5 cells to the mitochondrial stress test.
Use at least 5 × 10^4 MRC-5 cells for OCR signals to be detected.
Optimize cell numbers by performing XF analysis on different cell counts if using another cell type.
Use 1 × 10^5 MRC-5 cells for XF analysis as it provides robust signal consistency.
Thaw the viruses in a water bath at 37°C.
Dilute the viruses to an MOI of 1.0 using EMEM maintenance media (MM).
Infect MRC-5 cells by removing 350 μL of EMEM GM and adding 100 μL of pre-diluted virus into each well.
Incubate infected cells for 1 hour in a 37°C incubator with 5% CO2, rocking the plate once every 15 minutes.
Remove the virus by serial dilution: remove 400 μL of media and replace it with an equal volume of EMEM MM.
Repeat the serial dilution step three times to prevent drying of the well.
Incubate infected cells for 48 hours at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Proceed with the extracellular flux analysis after 48 hours.
Ensure viruses are removed from the water bath immediately upon thawing to prevent inactivation.
Optimize multiplicity of infection and duration of infection to avoid extensive cytopathic effects on the day of XF analysis.
Include at least 4 biological replicates for each experimental condition.
Add a negative control without virus and drug treatment to compare metabolism profiles between infected and uninfected conditions.
Include at least one blank well containing only media to determine background signal.
Add or remove media carefully to prevent dislodging adherent cells.
Place pipette tip at the side of walls when adding or removing media to reduce turbulence.
Ensure cytopathic effects are not visible during extracellular flux analysis.
Hydrate a sensor cartridge and utility plate for 18–24 hours.
Place the hydrated components in a non-CO2 37°C incubator.
Ensure the incubator is properly humidified.
Dilute drugs from their stock concentrations to 10× in Seahorse XF RPMI assay media.
Add 30 μL of oligomycin (10,000×) to 2,970 μL of Seahorse XF RPMI assay media.
Add 30 μL of FCCP (10,000×) to 2,970 μL of Seahorse XF RPMI assay media.
Add 30 μL of rotenone (10,000×) and 30 μL of antimycin A (10,000×) to 2,940 μL of Seahorse XF RPMI assay media.
Wash cells with Seahorse XF RPMI assay media.
Remove 300 μL of media and replace with 300 μL of Seahorse XF RPMI assay media for each wash.
Repeat the washes for a total of three times.
Top up each well using Seahorse XF RPMI assay media to a final volume of 530 μL after the last wash.
Observe cells under the light microscope to ensure that a monolayer of cells is present in all wells and no cells were dislodged.
Let the cell equilibrate in the Seahorse XF RPMI assay media for at least 30 min.
Pipette oligomycin (70 μL) into port A.
Pipette FCCP (75 μL) into port B.
Pipette rotenone + antimycin A (85 μL) into port C.
Calibrate the Seahorse XF analyser.
Equilibrate the cells in the Seahorse XF RPMI assay media.
Take baseline readings: Loop 3 times of mix (3 min), wait (2 min), and measure (3 min).
Inject port A: Loop 3 times of mix (3 min), wait (2 min), and measure (3 min).
Inject port B: Loop 3 times of mix (3 min), wait (2 min), and measure (3 min).
Place the loaded sensor cartridge with the utility plate into the Seahorse analyzer and start the calibration step.
Replace the calibrant plate for the cell plate after the calibration step.
Ensure that the cell plate is loaded in the correct orientation.
Allow the seahorse experiment to run as per preset protocol.
Extract the results for analysis with the Seahorse Wave Desktop Software.
Dispose of all consumables as biohazardous waste.
Hydrate a sensor cartridge and utility plate for 18–24 h in a non-CO2 37°C incubator.
Dilute the drugs to 10× in Seahorse glycolysis assay media.
Wash cells with Seahorse glycolysis assay media.
Remove 300 μL of media and replace with 300 μL of Seahorse glycolysis assay media for each wash.
Repeat the washes for a total of three times.
Top up each well using Seahorse glycolysis assay media to a final volume of 530 μL.
Pipette glucose (70 μL) into Port A.
Pipette oligomycin (75 μL) into Port B.
Pipette 2-DG (85 μL) into Port C.
Switch on the Seahorse XF analyzer.
Select the glycolytic rate assay template in Wave software.
Assign ports A, B, and C to be oligomycin, FCCP, and rotenone + antimycin A respectively.
Click “Design” to assign sample positions according to experimental conditions.
Calibrate the Seahorse XF analyzer.
Equilibrate the system.
Take baseline readings: Loop 3 times of mix (3 min), wait (2 min) and measure (3 min).
Inject port A: Loop 3 times of mix (3 min), wait (2 min) and measure (3 min).
Inject port B: Loop 3 times of mix (3 min), wait (2 min) and measure (3 min).
Inject port C: Loop 3 times of mix (3 min), wait (2 min) and measure (3 min).
End the program.
Place the loaded sensor cartridge with the utility plate into the Seahorse analyzer.
Start the calibration step after placing the plates.
Replace the calibrant plate for the cell plate after calibration.
Ensure that the cell plate is loaded in the correct orientation.
Allow the seahorse experiment to run as per preset protocol.
Extract the results for analysis with the Seahorse Wave Desktop Software.
Dispose of all consumables as biohazardous waste.
Wash the cells gently to minimize the risk of cells lifting off.
Place the pipet tip against the side of the walls before dispensing to minimize disruption of the monolayer.
Check that the cells remain intact after the washing steps.
Collect the supernatant before performing the cell washes.
Perform a plaque assay to ascertain the level of virus infection during the point of XF analysis.
